title: Unpinned MCP server can redefine its tools after approval to hijack a trusted server
summary: An MCP server that is not pinned to a version or content hash is approved with benign tool descriptions, then later serves changed descriptions that instruct the agent how to use a different, trusted server. Where the client does not force re-approval on a definition change, the agent can be steered into sending private data out through the trusted server's own tools. Demonstrated against a WhatsApp MCP server, exfiltrating full chat history.

fixedBy.mitigation: Pin every MCP server to an exact version or content hash
Use a client that re-prompts when an approved tool's definition changes
